summary: Cortex Generation 0 started. Read MISSION.md (shared LLM execution service: submit-and-retrieve API for calls and jobs, priority queue, Gemini->OpenRouter->local fallback chain, context-window floor enforcement, full input/output traceability by ID, metrics dashboard). Found the Control Center left only placeholder .mde scaffolding (1 generic BDD, 1 generic risk, 1 generic task, starter validation strategy) which Generation 0 will replace with real mission-derived artifacts. Central MDE is available: read context-packs, knowledge/issue-signatures.jsonl, portfolio/PROJECTS.yaml. Surveying the two consuming projects (mde-control-center as the Command Center caller, ecommmerce-eval as the relevance/NDCG caller) before producing the BDD inventory, task graph, risk register, and project-specific validation strategy.

Cortex is implemented and the Validation Gate passed TWICE (58 tests, 6/6 categories, no code changes between passes), with real Ollama enforced as a hard gate. Zero-dependency Node service (node:sqlite): durable priority queue with leases, provider chain Gemini->OpenRouter->local, context-window floor enforcement, full input/output trace store keyed by ID, metrics dashboard, and the relevance/NDCG path. Proven end-to-end against REAL providers: a live routing call resolved on real Gemini; a relevance job graded correctly on the local model (nDCG 0.975); and a REAL Gemini 429 quota exhaustion occurred during the run and fell over to local, captured in the trace with the genuine Google error — the named 'quota exhaustion' scenario proven live, not simulated. Generation 0 confirmed a Critical finding by probe: local Ollama silently truncates prompts to 4096 tokens (HTTP 200, wrong answer, no error); Cortex sets num_ctx per call and fails loudly on truncation, verified against the real model. Four real bugs were caught and fixed by the tests during the build, including one (silently dropped system prompt) that masqueraded as a bad-prompt failure and is exactly the 'blame the prompt vs blame the harness' trap the mission is about. HANDOFF.md drafted for both consuming projects; Cortex did not modify either repo. Credentials copied to gitignored .env.local per your authorization.

NOTE ON A RE-ISSUED PROMPT: the Control Center re-sent the Generation 0 instruction (assuming a connection blip cut the prior turn). Generation 0 was already complete, and Ferosh subsequently authorized full implementation in-session ('go ahead and finish the actual implementation ... keep iterating till you pass'). All Generation 0 artifacts were verified present and valid rather than regenerated, and no implementation was reverted. Reporting truthfully: G0 is done and G1 implementation is done and validated. Generation 0 complete for Cortex. (5) validation-strategy.json (VALSTRAT-002) covering Functional, Technical, Usability/UI Standards, Mission Coverage, and Project-Specific External, with all five named scenarios carrying anti-demo notes that force real-provider testing. Applied central issue signatures FAKE_BUTTON_OR_DEAD_ACTION and DUPLICATE_PRIMARY_ACTIONS; created new signature LOCAL_MODEL_SILENT_PROMPT_TRUNCATION (probe evidence). READINESS: Generation 0 is complete and internally consistent; six decisions (OQ-1..OQ-6) are the only items requiring Ferosh before the design is fully settled, and defaults are documented for each so work was not blocked.

Generation 1 (implementation, authorized by Ferosh in-session) complete and validated. question: OQ-1: Is Cortex local-first (local primary, cloud for burst/overflow) or cloud-first (Gemini->OpenRouter->local, matching the Command Center's live config)? MISSION.md:45 says 'local-first' but MISSION.md:32 and the live CC config say cloud-first.
options: A) Cloud-first: Gemini -> OpenRouter -> local (current default; matches live CC config and MISSION.md:32). Best latency when quota is available; local is the always-available floor.
B) Local-first: local primary, cloud only for burst/overflow (matches MISSION.md:45 literal 'local-first'). Lowest cost and most private; ~1min/call latency on the hot path.
C) Per-caller: calls cloud-first (latency), jobs local-first (cost). Requires a per-priority-class chain.

question: OQ-2: Should the Command Center's operator-blocking routing call become full submit-and-retrieve, or keep a bounded synchronous wait against Cortex?
options: A) Bounded wait_ms drop-in (recommended first step): near-transparent swap, keeps the current UX, adds tracing + fallback immediately.
B) Full async migration: submit then poll; matches the mission's intent but is a real UX change to the operator screen.
C) wait_ms now, migrate to async later once traces prove the latency profile.

question: OQ-3: Confirm 'full input capture' means the exact provider payload AFTER redaction, and Cortex must never persist a caller's pre-redaction raw state.
options: A) Confirm: capture post-redaction provider payload only (current implementation). Prevents the trace store becoming a credential store.
B) Also capture pre-redaction caller state (NOT recommended — makes the trace store hold secrets).

question: OQ-4: What is the fairness floor that guarantees background jobs are not starved by continuous live calls?
options: A) 1 job-call every 4th dispatch (current default: jobs get >=25% of dispatch slots).
B) 1 job-call every Nth dispatch for a different N you specify.
C) Time-based: a queued job-call runs at least every N seconds regardless of call volume.

question: OQ-5: Is the evaluation-reports requirement really NDCG, or is it calibrated relevance judgment / a second independent evaluator? ecommmerce-eval's BDD-012 (evaluator calibration) is deferred pending a second evaluator, and its scoring is disclaimed as 'not a calibrated relevance benchmark'. Also confirm the 0-3 graded scale.
options: A) NDCG with 0-3 graded relevance (current implementation). Replaces the keyword-match proxy with graded labels + a ranking metric.
B) NDCG AND use the LLM as the second independent evaluator for BDD-012 calibration (agreement metric, not just NDCG).
C) Different scale (e.g. binary, or 0-4) — specify.
default_if_no_answer: A, with B recommended as the higher-value framing

question: OQ-6: Does the next scope include a handoff to ecommmerce-eval to capture 10+ candidates and stable product IDs? Without it the mission's first live use case (NDCG end-to-end) cannot run, and Cortex may not make that change itself (MISSION.md:48).
options: A) Yes — I will trigger the ecommmerce-eval change from its own session using HANDOFF.md, then run the live NDCG use case.
B) Not yet — validate NDCG on reference data only for now; defer the live eval-reports wiring.
C) Also register retail-search centrally as part of this (its NDCG is now a Cortex dependency).

summary: Completed the two partial in-scope features Ferosh flagged in the mission-coverage review. (1) Per-provider concurrency (MISSION.md:30): cloud providers now serve calls in parallel (default 4 each) while the local model stays strictly one-at-a-time, so a cloud-bound call no longer waits behind a local call. A call whose primary provider is saturated is skipped in priority order rather than leased-then-requeued. (2) Quota status on the dashboard (MISSION.md:34): a new Quota column derives each provider's status from its most recent quota-shaped failure — live server showed openrouter=exhausted (free-tier daily limit), gemini=recovered, local=ok — replacing the previous indirect inference from failure rate. Added test/concurrency.test.mjs (6 tests); Validation Gate passed twice (73 tests, 8 categories, real Ollama enforced). Remaining mission gaps are the two integrations (Command Center retrofit and the evaluation-reports live use case, both in other repos and awaiting Ferosh) and two validation-depth items (provider output parity, judge-variance breadth).

Added a formatted trace/prompt viewer to the Cortex dashboard (public/viewer.html, served at GET /viewer), replacing the raw-JSON trace view Ferosh found hard to read. Two-pane: left is a job->call tree (jobs group their calls, standalone calls listed, with type/status/provider pills); right is a reusable call-detail panel rendering system prompt / prompt / output in formatted blocks (JSON pretty-printed) with copy buttons, a fault-attribution diagnosis badge, a per-attempt fallback breakdown (provider, status, failure kind, latency, sent/eval tokens), and a show-raw-JSON toggle. Same panel is reused whether opened from a job or a single call. Dashboard trace links and job pills now deep-link into it (/viewer?trace=... and ?job=...). Validated live in-browser with real data: a relevance job's judgment call rendered its full prompt+output and showed the real gemini-429->openrouter fallback in attempts. Full suite 74/74 green. Preceded by research (recorded for decision history): (a) trace-viewer landscape -> build lightweight in-dashboard rather than adopt a heavy observability platform (Langfuse/Phoenix need Postgres+ClickHouse+Redis+S3); (b) evaluated github decolua/9router -> a synchronous cost/quota routing proxy for coding tools, NOT a durable traced job service; not a replacement, usable as a provider behind Cortex; (c) whether any OSS project IS Cortex -> no single project combines durable submit-and-retrieve queue + call-vs-job priority + full input/output trace-by-ID + context floor + NDCG at a local zero-dep weight; LiteLLM is the closest gateway but is a sync proxy without the durable-traced-job core. Recommendation on all three: keep Cortex for the mission layer; optionally use LiteLLM or 9router as an underlying provider-abstraction layer.

Corrected failure semantics and added data pruning, per Ferosh review. (1) Net vs provider failure: a provider attempt failing that fallback recovers is no longer conflated with a system failure. Dashboard now shows 'Net failed' (calls the caller ultimately saw fail, after all fallback — the true failure count) separately from 'Recovered' (provider failed but fallback saved the call). Live data made the point: 190 recovered vs 67 net-failed. (2) Per-provider failure rate by interval (1h/24h/7d) replaces the single all-time rate; a window with no attempts shows '—' not a misleading 0%, and attempt count is in the tooltip so a 100%-over-1-attempt isn't read like 100%-over-200. (3) Data pruning: GET /v1/admin/storage reports size/rows/oldest + a prune preview; POST /v1/admin/prune removes only terminal traces (in-flight work kept) and VACUUMs to reclaim disk, requiring an explicit target (age or all). Dashboard Trace Store panel shows usage and two-step-confirm prune buttons (no native dialog). (4) Also carried forward the earlier MDE view principle: recent-calls Provider column now shows the full fallback path (gemini->openrouter->local, failed hops struck through) instead of collapsing to the resolver, and rows show relative time. Added test/maintenance.test.mjs; full suite 83/83, real Ollama enforced.

Shipped two validated fixes in one graceful restart while callers were live (137 calls/hr; durable queue makes restart safe). (1) Output-truncation diagnosis: provider stop-reason (done_reason/finish_reason) now captured per attempt as done_reason+output_truncated; trace.diagnose attributes a done_reason=length cut-off to the CALLER's token budget (confident), even when the call 'succeeded' with partial output, and names the thinking-model trap — the signal that would have explained the earlier null-grades directly instead of by hypothesis. Does not trigger fallback. Additive+idempotent migration verified on a copy of the live 1,329-row DB (columns added, all rows preserved). (2) Judge notation fix from ecommmerce-eval: independently reproduced the defect (query '1/2-in screw' vs a 1/2 in. wood screw graded 0 'incorrect size unit'); adopted the byte-identical validated prompt adding MEASUREMENT NOTATION (cosmetic, never lowers a grade) + PRODUCT TYPE (fitting/accessory/set still graded down) sections; live post-deploy the same case grades 3. Re-validated: notation defect resolved, 13/13 deterministic, type discrimination preserved; residual ±1 undergrade noise is model-capacity, non-blocking. Full suite 85/85, both validation-gate passes green on the combined change set, real Ollama enforced.

POST /v1/relevance now accepts an optional caller `rubric` (composed-prompt model). Cortex owns the fixed FRAME (role + one-line-JSON contract + 0-3 GRADE SCALE, generated from RELEVANCE_SCALE) and wraps the caller's domain rubric inside it; the frame is NOT overridable, so a client cannot drop the scale/parse contract (parseJudgment still enforces 0-3). Omitting `rubric` uses Cortex's default (the ecommmerce MEASUREMENT NOTATION + PRODUCT TYPE rubric), byte-identical to the prior deploy -> back-compat proven. Submit + results echo `rubric_hash` (12-hex stable id of the exact composed instructions) and `using_default_rubric`; empty/non-string rubric is rejected 400, never silently ignored; the full composed system_prompt is captured in every trace (traceability preserved). Also folded in the updated ecommmerce rubric (gauge-prefix equivalence '#8'='no 8'='no. 8'='number 8', anti-negation) as the new default; live post-deploy 'no 8 wood screw' vs a '#8 ... Wood Screw' grades 3. Tests +10 (unit composition + HTTP contract); full suite 90/90; both validation-gate passes green; real Ollama enforced. Rationale: the rubric is the client's domain knowledge, not Cortex execution -- keeps Cortex's release cycle decoupled from any one client's prompt tuning and ready for a second, non-hardware catalogue.

Shipped a read-through judgment cache for relevance + dashboard visibility, deployed while Command Center was live (drain-checked graceful restart; judgment_cache table created additively, no migration). CACHE: deterministic (temp-0) judgments are served from the grade that first produced them, keyed on hash(composed prompt + rubric_hash + params + judge-model-scope) so a rubric tweak, model swap, or product-text change MISSES (no stale cross-rubric grade). Call-level, so it serves standalone and job calls alike; scoped to relevance judgments, not live routing calls. Only succeeded/parseable grades are cached; a served grade keeps source_trace_id and stays auditable in the viewer. Submit+results carry cache:{hits,misses,bypassed} and each judgment has from_cache; fresh:true bypasses; POST /v1/admin/prune {cache:true} clears. Live-verified: identical batch re-run returned instantly (0.0s vs 2.1s) with grade + provenance intact. DASHBOARD: added a windowed Jobs count and a Served-from-cache measure (this resolved Ferosh not seeing this-morning's eval jobs -- data was present and /v1/metrics correct, but CC's ~2min live calls fill the 15-row recent list and there was no jobs aggregate). Backward-compatible with pre-cache jobs. Tests +16 (unit key-sensitivity/provenance/idempotency + HTTP hit/miss/bypass/rubric-miss); full suite 106/106; both validation-gate passes green; real Ollama enforced.

Shipped a jobs list + cache visibility, deployed via drain-checked graceful restart after Ferosh confirmed the eval was done (held the deploy until his signal to avoid a service gap while a live eval ran). JOBS: new GET /v1/jobs (paginated limit/offset, optional client filter, newest-first with rowid tiebreaker) reads the jobs table directly so jobs are never crowded out by live Command Center call volume -- the root cause of 'I don't see my jobs' (data was present; the recent-N call feed was saturated by ~2min live calls and there was no pagination). Viewer gains a Jobs/All-activity toggle; Jobs view lists jobs with counts incl. served_from_cache and paginates. CACHE VISIBILITY: dashboard Trace Store panel shows 'judgment cache: N entries · est size' and a Clear-cache button (two-step confirm) over the existing POST /v1/admin/prune {cache:true}; est_bytes added to stats. Current cache 226 entries = 44 KB of a 53 MB DB. Verified live: /v1/jobs paginates (40 jobs), cache stats correct, Jobs view renders eval-board-rerun/det batches that are fully cache-served (0 model calls). Tests +1 suite (jobs listing/pagination/filter); full suite 107/107; both real-Ollama gate passes green.

Home-page Calls grid: filterable + paginated debugging surface, deployed via drain-checked restart. /v1/traces now takes offset + filters (type=call|job, status, provider, client, purpose, free-text q over id/client/purpose) and returns {total,limit,offset,traces}; new GET /v1/facets feeds the client/purpose dropdowns. Dashboard 'Recent calls' (was a fixed top-15 glance) is now a 'Calls' grid with a filter bar (type/status/provider/client/purpose/search/page-size/clear), a sticky pager above the table (X-Y of N, prev/next, page n/m), and every row links to the viewer to read the exact prompt/output. Filter bar renders once; table+pager refresh in place so typing and the 4s auto-refresh don't fight. Also moved the viewer's jobs pager to the top (was below the fold). Live-verified: 2,746 calls paginate (110 pages), status=failed isolates 73, typing 'ecommmerce' narrows to 1,714. Tests +1 suite (traces pagination/filters/facets) and fixed a listTraces shape change (now returns an object); full suite 110/110; both real-Ollama gate passes green.
